records.text: White has a new passed pawn. Track the pieces that could block it; passed does not mean unstoppable.
Black has a new passed pawn. Track the pieces that could block it; passed does not mean unstoppable.
The better move would have produced a passed pawn for White. Compare the blockading options before choosing a route.
The better move would have produced a passed pawn for Black. Compare the blockading options before choosing a route.
White now has an isolated pawn. Scan the adjacent files: no friendly pawn. Then check its piece support.
Black now has an isolated pawn. Scan the adjacent files: no friendly pawn. Then check its piece support.
The better move would have left White with an isolated pawn. Include the missing neighboring pawns in the comparison.
The better move would have left Black with an isolated pawn. Include the missing neighboring pawns in the comparison.
White's pawns now share a file. Doubled structure. Check what changed around them.
Black's pawns now share a file. Doubled structure. Check what changed around them.
The better move would have doubled White's pawns. Evaluate that structure alongside the rest of the position.
The better move would have doubled Black's pawns. Evaluate that structure alongside the rest of the position.
White's rook now occupies a pawnless file. Open file. Trace its actual reach before planning an entry.
Black's rook now occupies a pawnless file. Open file. Trace its actual reach before planning an entry.
The better move would have placed White's rook on an open file. No pawns there; check the pieces next.
The better move would have placed Black's rook on an open file. No pawns there; check the pieces next.
White's rook has a half-open file: no friendly pawns, enemy pawns present. Check the lines between the rook and those pawns.
Black's rook has a half-open file: no friendly pawns, enemy pawns present. Check the lines between the rook and those pawns.
The better move would have given White's rook a half-open file. Locate the enemy pawns and test the placement.
The better move would have given Black's rook a half-open file. Locate the enemy pawns and test the placement.
White's knight has gained a defender. Find the new link; that is the pattern to retain.
Black's knight has gained a defender. Find the new link; that is the pattern to retain.
White's bishop was unguarded and now has support. Trace the new defensive connection.
Black's bishop was unguarded and now has support. Trace the new defensive connection.
White's rook is newly defended. Identify what now covers it before continuing the calculation.
Black's rook is newly defended. Identify what now covers it before continuing the calculation.
White's queen has picked up protection. Track that connection when considering the next move.
Black's queen has picked up protection. Track that connection when considering the next move.
The better move would have supplied a defender for White's knight. Compare the support links.
The better move would have supplied a defender for Black's knight. Compare the support links.
The better move would have guarded White's previously unsupported bishop. Identify the connection it would create.
The better move would have guarded Black's previously unsupported bishop. Identify the connection it would create.
The better move would have added protection to White's unguarded rook. Check that defensive link on the board.
The better move would have added protection to Black's unguarded rook. Check that defensive link on the board.
The better move would have covered White's undefended queen. Include that support in the comparison.
The better move would have covered Black's undefended queen. Include that support in the comparison.
White's knight has lost its last defender. Check possible attacks; an unguarded piece is not automatically lost.
Black's knight has lost its last defender. Check possible attacks; an unguarded piece is not automatically lost.
White's bishop is no longer defended. Mark the broken connection and test whether it matters tactically.
Black's bishop is no longer defended. Mark the broken connection and test whether it matters tactically.
White's rook has no defender after this move. Start the capture scan there; confirm before calling it a loss.
Black's rook has no defender after this move. Start the capture scan there; confirm before calling it a loss.
White's queen has lost its protection. Track the threats against it, without assuming a capture exists.
Black's queen has lost its protection. Track the threats against it, without assuming a capture exists.
The better move would have left White's knight without a defender. Test the attacks before rejecting the move.
The better move would have left Black's knight without a defender. Test the attacks before rejecting the move.
The better move would have removed the last defender of White's bishop. Check whether that bishop could actually be taken.
The better move would have removed the last defender of Black's bishop. Check whether that bishop could actually be taken.
The better move would have left White's rook unguarded. Compare the resulting threats, not just the missing cover.
The better move would have left Black's rook unguarded. Compare the resulting threats, not just the missing cover.
The better move would have stripped White's queen of its remaining protection. Test the position before assigning a cost.
The better move would have stripped Black's queen of its remaining protection. Test the position before assigning a cost.
Knight developed. First departure from its starting square. Check its next job.
The knight leaves its original square for the first time. Track its new connections.
A knight comes off its starting square. Development logged; now inspect the placement.
First outing for the knight. Identify what changes when it leaves its starting post.
Bishop developed. Its starting square is vacated for the first time. Trace its diagonals.
The bishop makes its first move from home. Check where it fits into the position.
A bishop leaves its original post. Development recorded; test the new placement.
First departure for the bishop. Mark the change from its starting square, then examine its job.
The better move would have developed a knight from its starting square. Compare its new post.
Knight development was the alternative. Its first move from home would have changed the piece layout; inspect that layout.
A knight could have left its original square with the better move. Test that placement against the game.
The better choice included the knight's first departure from its starting post. Put that development into the comparison.
The better move would have developed a bishop from its starting square. Trace the resulting diagonals.
The stronger choice included a bishop's first move from home. Compare its resulting placement with the game.
A bishop could have left its original square with the better choice. Check its role in that position.
The better option would have brought a bishop off its starting post for the first time. Examine the placement it would have reached.
Evaluation drops against the better choice. Compare the moves, then test the replies.
The engine prefers a stronger move. Focus the review on the difference between the resulting positions.
This choice gives up value relative to the best move. Run the comparison from here.
Position value lost against the stronger choice. Trace both reply sequences and locate the difference.
Capture available on the reply. Identify what can be taken, then check the exchange.
The other side can capture immediately. Trace that reply before moving deeper.
A capture is ready for the opponent. Check its consequences rather than assuming free material.
The next move can be a capture by the other side. Put it into the reply scan.
Error punished. You turned the opponent's previous mistake into something useful. Keep that response pattern.
The opponent slipped, and you made use of it. Identify the chance so it is easier to catch next time.
Good follow-through. You acted on the chance left by the opponent's last move.
Stronger option flagged. Locate the engine's move and test it against this one.
The engine favors an alternative. Test that move's replies alongside these.
Put the stronger engine choice on the board next and compare the results.
The passed pawn gains ground toward promotion. Track the blockers before the next push.
An existing passer moves closer to the last rank. Recheck its support and the route ahead.
The best reply checks the king. Start with the legal answers to that check.
King checked by the strongest reply. Calculate the responses before extending the line.
Lesson move matched. Keep the pattern in focus.
Target move hit. The lesson continues from this position.
That fits the lesson. Keep working through the idea.
Correct move. The puzzle continues; find the next step.
On target. Keep calculating the rest of the puzzle.
That step checks out. Stay with the puzzle for the next move.
Study move matched. Keep that position-to-move link.
Correct recall from the repertoire. Retain the starting position as well as the move.
That is the stored opening move. Keep the sequence in focus.
Best. Use this move as the reference when comparing the alternatives.
Exact choice. Now identify what makes it Best.
Good, with a stronger choice available. Compare once, then move on.
Sound move. The improvement is worth checking; this is Good rather than Best.
